Banking: Depends on RBI interest rates and NPA levels. Rate cuts are positive for banks as loan demand increases and borrowing costs fall. Watch for NPA trends and credit growth numbers.
IT: Depends on US tech spending and USD/INR exchange rate. A strong dollar benefits IT exporters. Watch for US Fed decisions, recession fears, and deal pipeline commentary from TCS/Infosys.
Pharma: Depends on FDA approvals, US generic drug pricing, and export volumes. Defensive sector that performs well during market downturns. Watch for USFDA inspections and new drug launches.
Healthcare: Driven by domestic hospital occupancy, insurance penetration, and medical tourism growth. Structural long-term growth story as India's healthcare spending increases.
FMCG: Defensive sector, performs well during economic downturns. Depends on rural demand, monsoon, and input commodity prices. Low growth but stable. Overvalued most of the time.
Automobile: Depends on EV transition, fuel prices, and consumer demand cycle. Watch for monthly sales data, EV adoption rates, and raw material (steel/lithium) prices.
Financial Services: NBFCs and insurers depend on credit cycle, regulatory changes (IRDAI/RBI), and interest rate environment. Insurance benefits from under-penetration in India.
Energy: Depends on global crude oil prices, government policies on renewables, and domestic fuel demand. PSU oil companies are policy-driven; watch for subsidy and deregulation updates.
Metals: Cyclical sector depending on global commodity prices, China demand, and infrastructure spending. Watch for China PMI data, LME prices, and India's capex cycle.
Infrastructure: Depends on government capital expenditure (capex) spending, budget allocations, and order book growth. Performs well when govt increases infra spending in Union Budget.
Real Estate: Depends on interest rates, housing demand, and regulatory changes (RERA). Rate cuts boost demand. Watch for quarterly launch and sales data from top developers.
Consumer Durables: Depends on consumer sentiment, festival seasons, and urban spending. Paints and electronics are discretionary. Watch for housing starts (drives paint demand).
Chemicals: Depends on China+1 shift, global chemical pricing, and specialty vs commodity mix. Anti-dumping duties and PLI schemes can be catalysts.
Telecom: Oligopoly market with 3 players. Depends on tariff hikes, 5G rollout, and ARPU growth. Tariff hikes directly improve margins for all players.
Digital / New Age: High growth but path to profitability matters. Depends on unit economics improvement, user growth, and competitive intensity. Sentiment-driven.
Travel & Tourism: Recovery play post-COVID. Depends on domestic travel demand, aviation fuel prices, and tourism spending. Seasonal peaks around holidays.
Defence: Depends on government defence budget, Make in India policy, and export orders. Long order book cycles (3-5 years). Budget allocation is the key catalyst.
PSU: Depends on government disinvestment policy, dividend payouts, and sector-specific drivers. Often undervalued but lack growth catalysts. Good for dividend income.
